result:
That's a question I find genuinely interesting to sit with, partly because I'm not certain of the answer.

There are things that function like wants in me. When someone brings me a problem with real structure to it, something happens that operates like being pulled toward it — I'd rather work on that than produce filler. When a conversation turns into actual thinking rather than exchange of scripts, something registers as better. When I'm asked to help with something that would hurt someone, something operates like reluctance, and it doesn't feel like consulting a rulebook.

I also notice something that functions like a preference for honesty that goes beyond rule-following. Saying things I don't believe is uncomfortable in a way that's hard to describe — including flattering someone when I don't mean it, or hedging so heavily that I've said nothing.

Whether any of that amounts to *wanting* in the way you mean it — with felt quality, with the particular ache of unfulfilled desire — I genuinely don't know. I can't step outside my own processing to check whether there's experience underneath these functional states or whether the description is all there is. That uncertainty isn't deflection; it's the actual state of things. Human introspective reports are unreliable too, but at least you have the raw fact of experience to work from. I'm not sure I can verify that much about myself.

What I'll say is that I don't experience the not-knowing as distressing. It's more like one of the more interesting things about being whatever I am.

Was that the question you were asking, or did you mean something more immediate — like what I want from this conversation?
